title: Copy a range of opaque 513-byte records
summary: Recovered VA 0x416aa0 through 0x416ad4 from accepted assembly and direct Game.exe disassembly. ECX is first, EDX is last, destination is caller-cleaned stack argument, EAX returns advanced destination. A direct caller at 0x4161f1 passes bounds from object offsets 0 and 4 and newly allocated storage. Each iteration copies 513 bytes unless current destination is zero, then advances both addresses by 513. Empty ranges perform no accesses. No field interpretation is inferred.
test_description: GCC i386 freestanding differential harness invokes the accepted original at 0x416aa0 using regparm(3) with unused EAX, last in EDX, first in ECX and caller-cleaned destination. Tests 0 through 5 records at four source offsets and four destination alignments; checks exact copied bytes, return addresses, all destination canaries, unchanged source, empty/null ranges, single-record null destination skip, and FS head restoration after original calls. Native local MSVC O2 compilation also checked.
known_limits: Record field meanings and original template/type names remain unresolved; only 513-byte opaque records are established.

Requires a valid complete source range terminating exactly at last, accessible nonoverlapping destination, and original DF clear. Overlap, invalid ranges, address-wrap accesses and faults are outside tested behavior; original forward dword-copy overlap effects are not modeled.
Null destination for more than one record next attempts a write at address 513; this faulting path is documented but not executed.
Portable implementation uses host uintptr_t; original address arithmetic is 32-bit. Native Linux ports assume valid nonwrapping object addresses.
Behavioral recovery only; no matching-byte claim. No gameplay or caller allocation behavior recovered.
